componentPlan.focusQuote: The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

overview.headline: Moon throw flies ballistic without drag

keyPoints.point: A thrown ball on the Moon feels no drag because there is no air
keyPoints.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyPoints.point: Horizontal speed stays unchanged through flight while ball moves sideways across ground
keyPoints.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.

keyPoints.point: Moon gravity is about 1.62 compared with 9.8 on Earth at roughly one sixth
keyPoints.quote: On the Moon g is about 1.62 m/s^2, roughly one sixth of the 9.8 m/s^2 we feel on Earth.

keyPoints.point: Putting time into height equation gives highest point for rising ball
keyPoints.quote: Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

keyTerms.gloss: absence of air resistance felt by thrown ball
keyTerms.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

keyTerms.gloss: force that pulls ball straight down
keyTerms.quote: The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its weight, which pulls it straight down.

keyTerms.gloss: steady rate that slows falling ball vertically
keyTerms.quote: Vertically, gravity slows the ball at a steady rate g.

analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers drag-free ballistic flight on the Moon, horizontal motion, vertical motion under lunar gravity, and maximum height compared with Earth.
analysis.subject: physics
